messages:
maria: FYI vuln-bot just flagged CVE-2026-1234 (libcrypto integer overflow) affecting our base inference image (rwinf/base:2026-02-28). It’s exploitable in TLS stacks used by our gRPC gateway.

vuln-bot: [automated] CVE-2026-1234 - libcrypto <= 1.3.5 - High - https://nvd.example/CVE-2026-1234 - affected packages: openssl/libcrypto (used in grpc native layer).

maria: Initial ask: do we backport to Dedicated + Private customer images, and if so what’s the minimal ship plan? Some customers run pinned private images and have offline update windows.

raj: tagging priority: this is High but exploit requires TLS handshakes with crafted payloads. We should treat Dedicated as P1 (SLA + shared infra), Private depends on customer risk profile. Recommend: P1 for hosted/dedicated, P2 for on-prem unless customer requests immediate backport.

courtney: on the private side we have two constraints: 1) some customers use customer-managed KMS and our image build step signs artifacts with SLSA2 attestations using our signing key. We can’t re-sign their pinned images without coordinating key exchange; 2) network-isolated clients need offline bundles. Both make a single push harder.

li: For Dedicated we can roll a hotfix image quickly: bump openssl -> 1.3.6, run unit/integration, push canary, then global. For Private: two options: (A) build a minimal rollback-friendly hotpatch layer that replaces the vulnerable libcrypto file, publish as patch image; (B) produce fully rebuilt customer images per their pinned tag. Option A is smaller but may break SLSA attestation assumptions.

sam: We should also consider RBAC change: private deploys currently block any image re-signing by our infra if customer KMS is set to external. We might need a short-term exception that allows our build service to create a separate signed hotfix artifact using customer provided ephemeral wrapping key. That requires audit logging and opt-in via support ticket.

maria: Agreed. Proposal: create a "hotfix-proc" flow: support ticket -> customer approves ephemeral wrap key (KMSEphemeral) or uploads signed bundle -> we produce patch image -> verifiable attestation + audit log. Documented and time-limited. Thoughts?

raj: Security okay with ephemeral wrap key if we capture full audit trail and limit lifetime. Need to update audit logging to record: who requested, customer org id, wrap-key id, build artifact id, SLSA attestation hash. Also add a field to the attestation: "hotfix: true".

courtney: Implementation notes: Build pipeline change to accept --ephemeral-wrap-key metadata, new job that outputs: image tar.gz + attestation.json + signature_by_customer_wrap. We'll need to add CLI hooks to the onprem updater so customers can apply the tar.gz without pulling from our registry.

li: For Dedicated timeline: can do code patch + canary deploy in ~6 hours assuming no test failures. For Private: per-customer rebuilds will take days per customer if done manually; hotpatch layer approach takes hours but requires careful validation.

maria: Action items:
- raj: update audit log schema + add "hotfix" flag (ETA 1 day)
- li: prepare minimal patch branch and CI (branch name: release/hotfix/openssl-2026-1234) (ETA 4 hours)
- courtney: spec ephemeral wrap flow + support ticket template + CLI apply instructions (ETA EOD)
- sam: list customers with pinned images / KMS external who should be proactively notified (ETA 2 hours)

sam: I'll also generate a risk matrix: customer uses TLS termination locally? high risk. exposure window. Will surface to AE to prepare outreach.

vuln-bot: Suggested CVE advisory text draft: "We have fixed CVE-2026-1234 in base images. Dedicated customers will see an automatic rollout. Private customers with pinned images should contact support to request a hotfix bundle or schedule a rebuild."

maria: One technical Q: do we need to change any RBAC permissions in onprem updater so customers can accept hotfixes without granting broad registry write?

courtney: Yes — add a specific "apply-hotfix" capability scoped to: org_id + image_tag. Minimal surface: no registry write, just local image install and attestation verification. That maps to existing installer role with one extra boolean flag. Requires doc changes.

raj: Don't forget KMS rotation implications. If customer uses envelope keys, the ephemeral wrap must be approved by KMS IAM. Support flow needs a signed IAM policy snapshot as part of ticket.

li: Testing plan for hotpatch:
1) unit + integration on our CI using HTTPTLS test harness
2) smoke test on Dedicated canary cluster (20 nodes)
3) sample offline apply on VM simulating air-gapped customer (we have one infra lab)
4) run full SLSA2 attestation verification against the rebuilt artifact

maria: Good. If CI green, we do Dedicated canary -> global. For Private, start outreach and offer hotpatch (fast) or full rebuild (recommended) depending on customer SLA window.

sam: I'll prep the customer email template: short, actionable, include steps for providing ephemeral wrap key and expected ETA.

maria: Any objections to the plan? If not, I'll file tracking issue and mark P1 for Dedicated.

raj: No objections. Also tag this for postmortem hooks: add a follow-up task to measure mean time to patch for private customers.

courtney: One more: coordinate with legal for customer consent language on ephemeral key usage.

maria: noted. I'll loop in legal.

deploy-bot: deploy job queued: release/hotfix/openssl-2026-1234 -> canary cluster (job 46233).

li: I'll watch the job and validate tests. Thanks everyone.

maria: Thanks — will update thread with ticket numbers and customer list when available. :white_check_mark:
